spans.s:
véda, m.
 —1. understanding, knowledge;
--2. esp. the sacred knowledge, handed
down in triple form of ṛc, yajus, and
sāman, see these, and cf. (trayī) vidyā;
--later, the well-known collections called
Rigveda, Yajurveda, and Sāmaveda
(635, 6), the holy scriptures, held to be a
revelation and so called śruti, 58^18.
[√1vid.]

vedá, m. tuft of strong grass (kuśa or
muñja) tied so as to form a broom, 62^18.

veda-nindaka, m. one who scoffs at
the Veda, infidel.

veda-puṇya, n. Veda-merit, sanctity
acquired by Veda-study.

veda-bāhya, a. being outside of the
Veda, i. e. extra-Vedic, differing from or
conflicting with the Veda. [1265, veda-
being in an abl. relation.]

1védas, n. knowledge; possibly adj.,
knowing, cf. na-vedas. [√1vid, ‘know’:
cf. 1151. 2a, b.]

2védas, n. (like Lat. quaestus) gettings,
property, cf. vitta. [√2vid, ‘get.’]

védi, f. sacrificial bed, i. e. a spot of ground
excavated two or three inches and covered
with straw and serving as a kind of altar.
vedi-purīṣa, n. loose earth of the vedi.
